```{python}
#| label: setup
import pandas as pd
import polars as pl
import holoviews as hv
import hvplot.pandas  # noqa: F401
from datetime import date, timedelta
from bokeh.models import NumeralTickFormatter
from IPython.display import HTML

# Loads BokehJS for the charts. Its empty output card is hidden in dashboard.scss.
hv.extension("bokeh")


def pdf(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """polars -> pandas without pyarrow, keeping dates as datetimes for the axis."""
    out = pd.DataFrame(df.to_dict(as_series=False))
    for col, dtype in df.schema.items():
        if dtype in (pl.Date, pl.Datetime):
            out[col] = pd.to_datetime(out[col])
    return out


class _Plotter:
    """frame.hvplot.<kind>(...) on a polars frame: converts it, and makes every chart
    stretch to fill its dashboard card (sizing has to be set when the plot is created)."""

    def __init__(self, df):
        self._hv = pdf(df).hvplot

    def __getattr__(self, kind):
        return lambda **kw: getattr(self._hv, kind)(**({"responsive": True, "min_height": 220} | kw))


# Analysis stays in polars; charts get a pandas copy at the last step.
pl.DataFrame.hvplot = property(_Plotter)

# Brand colors. Cobalt carries the story, gray is context, orange marks a decline.
COBALT, NAVY, MIST = "#1919e6", "#191970", "#8181fe"
GRAY, ORANGE, INK = "#a3a3bd", "#eb6834", "#15153f"
TALL = 440  # charts that own a full-height card
RAMP = ["#ffffff", "#cfcffe", MIST, COBALT, NAVY]
MILLIONS = NumeralTickFormatter(format="0.0a")
PCT = NumeralTickFormatter(format="0%")


def style(plot, **kw):
    """Shared chart chrome: recessive grid, no toolbar, consistent type sizes."""
    opts = dict(
        toolbar=None, show_grid=True,
        fontsize={"labels": "10pt", "ticks": "9pt", "legend": "9pt"},
        gridstyle={"grid_line_color": "#e6e6f5", "xgrid_line_alpha": 0},
    )
    return plot.opts(**(opts | kw))


def cell_labels(df, x, y, value, color_col):
    """Numbers printed on heatmap cells, dark text on light cells and white on dark."""
    return hv.Labels(pdf(df), kdims=[x, y], vdims=[value, color_col]).opts(
        text_font_size="8pt", text_color=color_col,
    )


def table(df, fmt=None):
    """Render a small polars frame as a styled HTML table."""
    fmt = fmt or {}
    head = "".join(f"<th>{c}</th>" for c in df.columns)
    rows = "".join(
        "<tr>" + "".join(f"<td>{fmt.get(c, str)(v)}</td>" for c, v in zip(df.columns, r)) + "</tr>"
        for r in df.iter_rows()
    )
    return HTML(f'<table class="dash-table"><thead><tr>{head}</tr></thead><tbody>{rows}</tbody></table>')


# ---- Data -------------------------------------------------------------------
tsa = (
    pl.read_csv("../../datasets/tsa.csv", try_parse_dates=True)
    .sort("Date")
    .with_columns(
        Year=pl.col("Date").dt.year(),
        Month=pl.col("Date").dt.month(),
        Weekday=pl.col("Date").dt.strftime("%a"),
        DayOfYear=pl.col("Date").dt.ordinal_day(),
        MA28=pl.col("Passengers").rolling_mean(28),
        MA7=pl.col("Passengers").rolling_mean(7),
        # 364 days back lands on the same weekday, so Fridays compare with Fridays.
        LastYear=pl.col("Passengers").shift(364),
    )
)
LAST = tsa["Date"].max()
CUR = LAST.year
fmt_m = lambda v: f"{v / 1e6:,.2f}M"
fmt_pct = lambda v: f"{v:+.1f}%"

annual = tsa.group_by("Year").agg(Passengers=pl.sum("Passengers"), Days=pl.len()).sort("Year")
growth = annual.with_columns(Growth=(pl.col("Passengers") / pl.col("Passengers").shift(1) - 1) * 100)
g24 = growth.filter(pl.col("Year") == 2024)["Growth"][0]
g25 = growth.filter(pl.col("Year") == 2025)["Growth"][0]

# Year to date on matching weekdays: each 2026 day against the same weekday in 2025.
ytd = tsa.filter(pl.col("Year") == CUR)
ytd_change = (ytd["Passengers"].sum() / ytd["LastYear"].sum() - 1) * 100
```

# Pandemic & Recovery

```{python}
#| label: recovery-data
base = tsa.filter(pl.col("Year") == 2019).group_by("Month").agg(Base=pl.mean("Passengers"))
recovery = (
    tsa.filter(pl.col("Year") >= 2020)
    .group_by("Year", "Month").agg(Avg=pl.mean("Passengers"))
    .join(base, on="Month")
    .with_columns(
        Recovery=pl.col("Avg") / pl.col("Base"),
        MonthStart=pl.date(pl.col("Year"), pl.col("Month"), 1),
        MonthName=pl.date(2000, pl.col("Month"), 1).dt.strftime("%b"),
    )
    .sort("MonthStart")
)
trough = tsa.sort("Passengers").row(0, named=True)

# First month after which demand never again fell more than 2% short of 2019.
first_full = (
    recovery.with_columns(ok=(pl.col("Recovery") >= 0.98).reverse().cum_min().reverse())
    .filter(pl.col("ok")).row(0, named=True)
)
y2019 = annual.filter(pl.col("Year") == 2019)["Passengers"][0]
lost = 3 * y2019 - annual.filter(pl.col("Year").is_between(2020, 2022))["Passengers"].sum()
```

# Travel Seasonality

```{python}
#| label: season-data
post = tsa.filter(pl.col("Year") >= 2023)  # fully recovered years only
order = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
months = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"]
overall = post["Passengers"].mean()
wd = (
    post.group_by("Weekday").agg(Avg=pl.mean("Passengers"))
    .with_columns(Index=pl.col("Avg") / overall - 1)
    .with_columns(pl.col("Weekday").cast(pl.Enum(order))).sort("Weekday")
    .with_columns(pl.col("Weekday").cast(pl.Utf8))
)
hm = (
    post.with_columns(MonthName=pl.col("Date").dt.strftime("%b"))
    .group_by("MonthName", "Weekday").agg(Avg=pl.mean("Passengers"))
    .with_columns(
        AvgM=(pl.col("Avg") / 1e6).round(2),
        Ink=pl.when(pl.col("Avg") < 2.3e6).then(pl.lit(INK)).otherwise(pl.lit("#ffffff")),
    )
)
mon = post.group_by("Month").agg(Avg=pl.mean("Passengers")).sort("Avg")
slow, peak = wd.sort("Avg").row(0, named=True), wd.sort("Avg").row(-1, named=True)
swing = (peak["Avg"] / slow["Avg"] - 1) * 100
low_m, high_m = months[mon["Month"][0] - 1], months[mon["Month"][-1] - 1]
month_swing = (mon["Avg"][-1] / mon["Avg"][0] - 1) * 100
```

# Demand & Anomalies

```{python}
#| label: anomaly-data
def nth_weekday(y, m, wd, n):
    d = date(y, m, 1)
    return d + timedelta(days=(wd - d.weekday()) % 7, weeks=n - 1)


def last_weekday(y, m, wd):
    d = date(y, m + 1, 1) - timedelta(days=1)
    return d - timedelta(days=(d.weekday() - wd) % 7)


def holiday_near(d):
    """Name the travel holiday a date falls near, or None for an ordinary day."""
    y = d.year
    windows = {
        "Thanksgiving": (nth_weekday(y, 11, 3, 4), 6),
        "Memorial Day": (last_weekday(y, 5, 0), 4),
        "Labor Day": (nth_weekday(y, 9, 0, 1), 4),
        "Presidents' Day": (nth_weekday(y, 2, 0, 3), 4),
        "MLK Day": (nth_weekday(y, 1, 0, 3), 3),
        "Columbus Day": (nth_weekday(y, 10, 0, 2), 4),
        "Independence Day": (date(y, 7, 4), 3),
        "Halloween": (date(y, 10, 31), 1),
    }
    for name, (anchor, span) in windows.items():
        if abs((d - anchor).days) <= span:
            return name
    if (d.month == 12 and d.day >= 18) or (d.month == 1 and d.day <= 5):
        return "Christmas / New Year"
    return None


def holiday_label(d):
    """A holiday on the day itself, or on the day it is compared with a year earlier."""
    return holiday_near(d) or holiday_near(d - timedelta(days=364))


# Expected = same weekday last year, scaled by how the last 28 days compared with a year
# earlier. This keeps seasonality (January lulls are normal) and the current trend.
THRESHOLD = 0.15
anom = (
    tsa.with_columns(
        Trend=pl.col("Passengers").shift(1).rolling_sum(28)
        / pl.col("LastYear").shift(1).rolling_sum(28)
    )
    .with_columns(Expected=pl.col("LastYear") * pl.col("Trend"))
    .with_columns(Deviation=pl.col("Passengers") / pl.col("Expected") - 1)
    .filter(pl.col("Year") >= 2024)  # 2023 compares with a still-recovering 2022
    .with_columns(Holiday=pl.col("Date").map_elements(holiday_label, return_dtype=pl.Utf8))
    .with_columns(
        Flag=pl.when(pl.col("Deviation").abs() < THRESHOLD).then(None)
        .when(pl.col("Holiday").is_not_null()).then(pl.lit("Holiday shift"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit("Unplanned"))
    )
)
flagged = anom.filter(pl.col("Flag").is_not_null())
unplanned = flagged.filter(pl.col("Flag") == "Unplanned")
share_plannable = (1 - unplanned.height / flagged.height) * 100
worst = unplanned.sort("Deviation").row(0, named=True)
```

or the day it is compared with, falls near a holiday.</p>
<p><strong>{share_plannable:.0f}% of the big swings are plannable from the calendar.</strong>
Only the orange days, led by the late January 2026 winter storm, need a contingency plan.</p>

# Year over Year

```{python}
#| label: yoy-data
yoy = (
    tsa.filter(pl.col("Year") >= 2024)
    .with_columns(MonthStart=pl.col("Date").dt.truncate("1mo"))
    .group_by("MonthStart").agg(pl.sum("Passengers"), pl.sum("LastYear"))
    .sort("MonthStart")
    .with_columns(
        YoY=pl.col("Passengers") / pl.col("LastYear") - 1,
        Label=pl.col("MonthStart").dt.strftime("%b %y"),
    )
    .with_columns(Color=pl.when(pl.col("YoY") >= 0).then(pl.lit(COBALT)).otherwise(pl.lit(ORANGE)))
)
neg_streak = yoy.reverse().select((pl.col("YoY") < 0).cast(pl.Int8).cum_min().sum()).item()
worst_month = yoy.sort("YoY").row(0, named=True)

gap = (
    tsa.filter(pl.col("Year") == CUR)
    .with_columns(Gap=(pl.col("Passengers") - pl.col("LastYear")).cum_sum())
)
gap_now = gap["Gap"][-1]
gap_peak = gap.sort("Gap").row(-1, named=True)
```

<div class="takeaways small">
<p>{CUR} was running <strong>{gap_peak['Gap'] / 1e6:.1f}M passengers ahead</strong> of 2025 in
{gap_peak['Date']:%B}. From April on, every month came in lower than a year earlier, the worst being
